### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**3** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a386a1d883d0a0f43535ee248122593278c7cc3a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9c597e68d60ea6ac097773342895121d17d92f75` — the merge of head `c4494a60c2a194d7b4e872b39482ff00a9310b51` into base `a386a1d883d0a0f43535ee248122593278c7cc3a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9c597e68d60ea6ac097773342895121d17d92f75 && git checkout 9c597e68d60ea6ac097773342895121d17d92f75
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a386a1d883d0a0f43535ee248122593278c7cc3a c4494a60c2a194d7b4e872b39482ff00a9310b51 && git checkout -B drift-repro a386a1d883d0a0f43535ee248122593278c7cc3a && git merge --no-ff c4494a60c2a194d7b4e872b39482ff00a9310b51

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a386a1d883d0a0f43535ee248122593278c7cc3a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c171abb9bbf2e286d0b7a5f1d268d35f193f6930`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/package-unmanaged-install.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/package-unmanaged-install.test.ts (the narrowing face: every path of the diff outside the prose faces; the changeset under ② only) + read, not reviewed: packages/spec/src/kernel/namespace-prefix.ts (`validateObjectNamespacePrefix`, `deriveNamespaceFromPackageId`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/package-namespace-rename.ts (`planNamespaceRename`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save-door-refusals.ts (`objectNamespacePrefixViolation`), packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts (the door's call), docs/adr/0048-cross-package-metadata-collision.md §3.5, content/docs/deployment/install-modes.mdx, .changeset/35823-unmanaged-derived-namespace-mismatch.md

### ① Derived judgments

Inputs read: card #36166 body and all 8 comments, PR #37065 body and file list (3 files), the net diff against `main`, the check-runs on the head. Every check-run on the head is success or skipped by its selector; the one `cancelled` Check Changeset run (05:58Z) is superseded by a success run at 06:02Z. Test Core 1/10 to 10/10, Type Check (4 lanes), Build Core, Dogfood Regression Gate, Lint lanes, PR-body guards: success.

Accept-set changes the diff implies, on the rename path only (`targetNamespace` differing from the source namespace), each read in the tree:

- **Namespace-less body, no object carrying the derived prefix, a group of two or more object names sharing a first segment, other objects beside it**: was renamed in front, now `400 INVALID_REQUEST` naming the group's objects. Right: the `every(...)` early return is gone, names are grouped by first segment, groups of one are skipped. The all-sharing case (#36138) is the same code path with the same sentence (`begins`), so its pin holds unchanged.
- **Namespace-less body, a single object**: unchanged (rename in front). Right: the `length < 2` guard is subsumed by the group-size guard; the pin keeps its assertion.
- **Namespace-less body, one object carrying the derived prefix**: unchanged, nothing refused. Right: the first line returns before grouping.
- **Declared `namespace`, any object name `validateObjectNamespacePrefix` refuses under it** (foreign prefix, bare name, legacy `ns__short` form): was renamed (in front, or prefix-swapped for the `__` form), now `400 INVALID_REQUEST` naming each such object. Right as to mechanism: the judge and the namespace argument are the ones the save door passes for a non-rename install (`objectNamespacePrefixViolation` reads the base manifest's namespace, which without a rename is the declared one), so the rename path refuses exactly the names the non-rename path refuses with `422 NAMESPACE_PREFIX`, no more. `sys_*` names stay exempt on both.
- **Declared `namespace`, a bare name whose copy name a prefixed sibling claims** (`lead` beside `crm_lead`): still `400 INVALID_REQUEST` naming `lead`, but by the declared-prefix refusal, which is raised first; the collision sentence is now reached from namespace-less bodies (and `sys_*` names) only. Right: same code, status and refused name; the fixture was moved to a namespace-less body and still pins the collision branch.
- **Public surface**: no export, schema key, envelope key or error code is added or changed; `declaredNamespaceContradiction` is module-private; one new import of an existing spec export. Right.

### ② Semver level

`'@objectstack/metadata-protocol': patch`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, `Ruling-ref: #36166 comment 7146137652`, and the `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker. The PR body carries the same three lines. Not re-ruled. Check Changeset on the head: success. The diff publishes no new export or schema shape, so nothing in it asks for a level above the ruled one.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Report 7139917764, `open_questions` (the declaration pair, A or B): answered by the maintainer ruling recorded in 7146137652 (B); the changeset and PR body at this head carry B. The withdrawn correction pair 7139969130 / 7140001966 is superseded by that ruling.
- Report 7139917764, three gate families NOT MEASURED locally (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure`, `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test`): answered by the head's check-runs (Build Core, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, Lint · repo & tooling gates: success).
- Reports 7139917764 and 7148766924, out-of-scope notes (the dispatch's model-named commit trailer; the relay's signed-trailer position in the PR body): process notes with no effect on the diff; no carrier owed by this review.
- Reports 7148766924 and 7154330642: `open_questions` empty.
- Card Done-when, the ADR half (the dated §3.5 note and the case-1 decision "recorded on the ADR"): not in this diff by the claim's file surface. The PR says `Part of #36166`, so the card stays open as the carrier; the note text is in the PR body. Not a finding on this head; the card must not close on this merge.
- For the maintainer's approval read (the PR's own "Read first" 2): the group signal refuses an honest namespace-less package whose two-word names repeat a first word beside other objects (`sales_order`, `sales_invoice`, `customer`), which before copied uniformly under the target. This is the #36138 family extended as the card's case 2 wrote it (`purchase_order` named as a stray there), so it is not graded against the dev; see S2 for what the refusal then tells that package.
- SQL push-down: none in play. Both functions are pure, over the object names of the manifest in memory; no query, no id materialisation, no in-app join.
- PR author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.

### ④ Design judgment

**packages/metadata-protocol/src/package-unmanaged-install.ts**

- Holds against the cited code. `validateObjectNamespacePrefix` is the one judge `defineStack` and the save door ask (`stack.zod.ts`, `protocol-save-door-refusals.ts`), it skips an empty namespace as the docblock says, and the door (`marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts`) passes the package body as declared, so a namespace-less body reaches the derived branch and a declared one the new branch. Both refusals are thrown inside `planUnmanagedImport`, before the base exists, through the existing `unmanagedInstallRenameRefusal` envelope.
- Break attempts that did not break it: a derived-prefix carrier beside a foreign group (cleared, first line); a name with no separator (in no group); a derived namespace containing `_` (a name carrying it returns on the first line, so no group can be the derived namespace); the case-3 judge against the non-rename install (same judge, same namespace: nothing refused on the rename path that the save door accepts).
- S1 (should-fix) — the hand-written public page for this door, `content/docs/deployment/install-modes.mdx` ("Rename on install"), is left teaching the pre-PR answers. Its refusal table row reads "two or more objects whose names all begin with the same first word", which the group signal no longer requires; it has no row for a declared `namespace` the object names do not carry; and its rule "an object whose name lacks the package's prefix takes the new one in front (`ticket` copies as `acme_ticket`)" is now true of a namespace-less package only, while a package declaring `crm` gets `400 INVALID_REQUEST` for `ticket`. The PR body states the tree was not read. The changeset's second bullet shows only the foreign-prefix example and should name the bare-name case too, since that is the one the page and ADR-0048 §3.5 spell out. Fix: update the page's bullet and table in this PR (hand-written tree, not auto-generated), or name a carrier card for it before the queue.
- S2 (should-fix) — the stray-group refusal prescribes a fix the same planner refuses on the next attempt. For `demoasset_asset`, `demoasset_site`, `site` the reason ends "Declare `namespace` on the package, the prefix its object names carry, then install again"; with `namespace: 'demoasset'` declared, `declaredNamespaceContradiction` refuses `site`. With two groups (`a_x`, `a_y`, `b_x`, `b_y`) each group is told to declare its own prefix. The sentence was complete when every object shared the prefix (#36138); for a partial group it is one step short, and for the honest package in ③ the real remedy (every object named under the declared namespace) is never stated on the first refusal. Fix: on the partial-group arm, say that the other object names must carry the declared namespace too; the changeset's closing line ("declare ... or name each object ...") wants the same "and".
- N1 (nit) — the docblock sentence "Without a rename the save door's own prefix rule refuses the same names" is kept on `derivedNamespaceContradiction`; it is accurate, but the stray of a refused group is also refused there, which the sentence's "same names" understates.
- N2 (nit) — on the derived path two or more `sys_*` object names form a group and are refused with "declare `namespace`", while the declared path's judge exempts `sys_*`. Inherited from #36138's signal; only the stray case is new.
- N3 (nit) — a body that writes the id-derived namespace out as `namespace` is judged declared, so the single-object and no-shared-segment shapes "decided to stay" are refused for it. Consistent with "declared is declared"; worth one clause in the ADR note.

**packages/metadata-protocol/src/package-unmanaged-install.test.ts**

- Holds against the card's three cases: case 1 pinned as the rename (retitled DECIDED, assertion unchanged); case 2 pinned at the planner for both strays the card names (`site`, `purchase_order`) and at the verb with `writes`, `packages` and `sys_metadata` empty; case 3 pinned at the planner (all refused, partial, bare name) and at the verb with zero writes, plus the non-rename control at `422 NAMESPACE_PREFIX`. Every refusal test asserts status and code together and the refused names by exact list; the only prose asserted is the namespace and prefix tokens inside `reason`, which is where the envelope carries them. The removed half of the declared CONTROL is the answer that changed, and it reappears as a refusal pin, so no pin was dropped.
- N4 (nit) — no test has two refused groups in one body, so the final sort back into manifest order (the only reason the sort exists) is unpinned.

No must-fix. S1 and S2 are should-fix and each owes a delta review of its fix.
